finding: First-innings win-probability model is mis-shaped early in the innings: a wicket on ball 1 costs about 8 pp and a powerplay dot costs about 2 pp. Innings-1 leverage is therefore highest in overs 1-6 and falls through the innings. First-over balls score Medium (mean PI about 70). The checkpoint lists this as 'surprising' but does not explain it.
evidence: Model 2023 and 2026: P(win) at 0 wkts / 119 balls left = 0.561 / 0.527; with 1 wkt = 0.480 / 0.463. Mean WPA of an innings-1 wicket: over 1 -0.083, over 10 -0.063, over 16 -0.047, over 20 -0.021. Mean WPA of a powerplay dot ball -0.018 to -0.021. Mean leverage, innings 1: over 1 0.0175, over 15 0.0103, over 18 0.013 (innings 2 over 12: 0.012). Mean PI over 1 = 69.8. Cause: INN1_FEATURES (wkts_in_hand, wk_x_balls, runs_vs_par) enter the logit linearly. Inn-1 Brier 2023 0.2476 (no better than a constant) and 2026 0.2404. Ran models in data/work/wp_models.pkl.
suggested_fix: Cap early-innings sensitivity: use a flatter or saturating form (for example balls_left x wickets bins, or a monotone spline), or shrink innings-1 WP toward 0.5 when many balls remain. Re-check that a first-over wicket costs about 2-4 pp. Re-run 1b; explain or fix the 'Medium at over 1' effect. Alternatively state the innings-1 leverage and WPA as unreliable.

finding: Win probability is overconfident in the last overs of a chase, which is where High pressure and the WPA for the most important balls sit. The overall calibration table hides this.
evidence: Chase balls with <=6 balls left, 2023-26 pooled (n=842 balls): predicted 0.610 -> observed 0.368 (34 balls, 22 matches); 0.812 -> 0.574 (61 balls, 33 matches); 0.974 -> 0.880 (142 balls, 56 matches). Model check: need 1 off 1 ball, 1 wkt in hand gives P=0.94 (2023 model) and 0.93 (2026 model), although a dot ball is a tie at best. Observed rates have wide ball-level error bars (balls from the same match are correlated), but all three bins are below the predictions.
suggested_fix: Add an end-game term or a separate last-2-overs model, or simply a flexible form in required rate and balls left. Report calibration by balls-left band (<=12 / 13-36 / more). Until then, qualify any statement that rests on late-chase leverage or WPA.

finding: WPA for byes and leg-byes does not follow the approved G5 rule ('credit the batter with the full change') and is not logged anywhere. The batter is given the counterfactual of a dot ball. The bowler is also credited a dot ball. The change from the byes is credited to no one. When the byes win the match, the batter is debited and the bowler credited.
evidence: From pressure_ball: byes/leg-byes = 994 balls in 2023-26, 23% High. Sum of unassigned |WPA| 3.36 (byes) + 10.36 (leg-byes). Match 50139 ball 127: wp 0.972 -> 1.000 on a bye, wpa_batter = -0.472, wpa_bowler = +0.472. Match 20195 ball 129: wp 0.941 -> 1.000, wpa_batter = -0.441. Match 20181 ball 115 (leg-byes, 4): wpa_ball +0.135, wpa_batter -0.069. G5 text is in docs/FRAMEWORK_REVIEW.md line 114. Code: step1b_pressure.py lines for wp_bat / wp_bowl. No entry in DEFINITIONS or DATA_NOTES.
suggested_fix: Follow G5: batter gets the full change (wp_after - wp_before) on byes/leg-byes. Bowler gets the change minus byes/leg-byes. Log the rule in DEFINITIONS, with the run-out and wide-wicket rules.

finding: Win-probability feature set was changed (D26) after looking at the 2023-26 test results, and the change made 3 of 4 seasons worse. The out-of-sample Brier is therefore no longer a clean test, and the checkpoint describes it as 'simplified' without saying so.
evidence: step1a_wp_eval vs step1a_wp_eval_v1_with_par_feature: Brier 2023 0.2353 -> 0.2173 (better); 2024 0.1648 -> 0.1665; 2025 0.1667 -> 0.1689; 2026 0.1677 -> 0.1831 (9% worse; 2026 innings 1 0.2274 -> 0.2404). Pooled 0.18397 -> 0.18422, i.e. no gain. The choice was driven by the 2023 fold (one training season). D19 requires a model change only on the basis of earlier folds.
suggested_fix: State in CHECKPOINTS and D26 that the specification was chosen after seeing the test seasons, and that 2024-26 are slightly worse. Preferably show the v1 versus v2 comparison next to the main table. Do not tune further.

finding: Step 2 expected runs still carry a persistent, large innings-and-phase offset that the checkpoint and D28 do not mention. Only season means are reported. Innings 1 batters beat expectation by far more than chasers. This feeds directly into the 'chasing vs setting' split and the High-minus-Low 'pressure drop' (High balls are mostly innings 2).
evidence: Mean RAE per ball faced 2023-26 by innings and phase (expected_ball.parquet): innings 1 Death +0.060, Middle +0.025, Powerplay +0.025; innings 2 Death +0.004, Middle +0.006, Powerplay +0.004. Bowler RSE per delivery: innings 1 Death -0.036, Middle -0.011, PP -0.014; innings 2 about -0.0003 to -0.015. step2_phase_offsets.csv is by season and phase only, not by innings. Intra-season: 2024 matches 31-45 +0.149, 61-80 -0.056.
suggested_fix: Add innings to the season factor (innings x phase x season, which was meant by D28 but did not remove it), or report/correct the offset. Add step2_innings_phase_offsets.csv, and warn Step 3/4 that chase vs setting and pressure drop are biased by about 3-5 runs per 100 balls.

finding: Checkpoint 1 says 'WPA adds up exactly', but the check only shows that wp_after equals the next ball's wp_before. This is true by construction: the same model and the same function produce both. Batter + bowler WPA do not add up to the ball's WPA for byes, leg-byes, run-outs, wides (batter) or a stumping off a wide.
evidence: My check: within-innings wp_after vs next wp_before has 0 mismatches of 79,806, and the innings handover 333/333 is exact. Batter and bowler residuals (wpa_ball - wpa_batter, wpa_ball + wpa_bowler): non-zero on 175 byes, 1,009 leg-byes, 226 run-outs (95/189 balls), 3,302 wides (batter 0 by construction), and 20 wide-with-wicket balls. Totals 2023-26: sum of wpa_batter +5.6; sum of -wpa_bowler +40.6 (about -29 of it from wides).
suggested_fix: Reword the checkpoint line: 'ball-level win-probability chain is consistent; player credit leaves X of unassigned WPA'. Add a reconciliation table: total WPA = batter + bowler + non-striker + unassigned, by cause.

finding: High-pressure share by innings and season is very uneven: the D27 scale equalises only the overall share. Because each season's model has its own leverage scale, 'High' means different things in each season, and the players' High samples inherit that.
suggested_fix: Report the High share by innings per season in the checkpoint. Consider scaling within innings, or flag the 2023 model (one training season) as lower quality in all pressure summaries.

finding: 2023 calibration is poor (overconfident at the extremes) and Checkpoint 1 does not say so. The master prompt says to say so and simplify. The checkpoint only mentions that first-innings skill is low.
evidence: step1a_calibration.csv, 2023: predicted 0.032 -> observed 0.148 (80% interval 0.086-0.214); 0.147 -> 0.324 (0.243-0.421); 0.353 -> 0.529 (0.437-0.610); 0.647 -> 0.527 (0.458-0.600); 0.851 -> 0.699 (0.620-0.782); 0.962 -> 0.850 (0.783-0.923). 7 of 10 bins have the diagonal outside the 80% interval. 2023 all-ball Brier 0.2173 with 80% interval 0.1885-0.2494, which includes the coin flip. CP1 never states that the 2023 model uses only one earlier season (D10 disclosure).
suggested_fix: Add one line to Checkpoint 1: 2023 model is overconfident (list of bins), trained on 67 matches. Add the D10 disclosure to every pressure output for 2023.

finding: The chase-pressure boost saturates at its maximum at the start of every chase because the current run rate is 0 on the first balls.
evidence: step1b_pressure.py: chase_pressure = clip((rrr - crr)/6, 0, 1) with crr = 0 when legal_balls_before = 0. First ball of the chase: mean boost 0.996 (min 0.633). Mean boost by over: over 1 0.60, over 2 0.39, over 6 0.22; 19% of all chase balls have boost = 1.0. The boost then adds up to 10% to leverage on those balls.
suggested_fix: Use a floor for balls faced (for example, blend crr with the par rate over the first 2-3 overs), or drop the boost when legal_balls_before < 12.

finding: A wide with a wicket (stumping or run-out) never charges the batter in WPA: wpa_batter is set to 0 for every wide.
evidence: 20 balls in 2023-26 (14 Stump, 6 RunOut), wpa_batter = 0 on all 20, wpa_ball sum -1.14, 7 of them High. Code: np.where(is_wide, 0.0, wp_bat - wp_before).
suggested_fix: For a wide: keep the batter's WPA at 0 for the runs, but still charge the dismissal when the batter is out. Log the rule.

finding: The metric glossary is empty and the WPA, leverage and boost rules are only described in script docstrings. Part 5 and Golden Rule 5 require every new metric in DEFINITIONS the moment it is introduced. The docstring in step1b says 'see DEFINITIONS', which has no such entry.
evidence: logs/DEFINITIONS.md section D: '(none yet)'. Missing: win probability, leverage, Pressure Index, buckets, WPA (batter/bowler/non-striker), RAE, RSE, wicket-above-expected, season factor, opposition factor. Missing from logs: the WPA assignment decision (G5 says 'log this'); the playoff derivation is only in Part B.
suggested_fix: Add the glossary lines and the WPA assignment table to DEFINITIONS section D.

finding: The main index is nearly the same as the leverage-only one, so the three 'definitions' amount to two. The boost weights (all 0.1) were not tested for effect. The 'close-game' variant also changes nothing.
evidence: step1b_definition_overlap_balls.csv: Spearman(raw main, raw leverage-only) = 0.989; share of main High also High in leverage-only 84.3%; with close-game boost 98.7% (rho 0.9996); rule-based 30.1% (rho -0.026). Boost correlations on the 2022 reference: -0.071 to +0.081, all 'kept' at weight 0.1 (no rule can reduce a weight that is already independent).
suggested_fix: State plainly in the checkpoint that the context boosts barely move the ranking, and that the real robustness test is main vs rule-based. Consider whether the boosts earn their place.

finding: The GBM comparison is a weak challenger and the old v1 table left in outputs/tables shows a broken GBM.
evidence: HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=200, lr=0.05, 15 leaves) with no tuning, no early stopping, no monotone constraints, and ball rows (correlated) from 67 matches in 2023. v2: GBM Brier 0.269 (inn 1) and 0.210 (inn 2) in 2023, worse than a coin flip for innings 1. v1 file step1a_gbm_comparison_v1_with_par_feature.csv has GBM Brier 0.461-0.483 in innings 1 (it memorised the season-level par). Ties dropped for GBM, kept at half weight for LR. 'GBM was worse in every fold' is true but weak evidence.
suggested_fix: Say 'an untuned GBM overfits at this sample size' rather than 'LR is better'. Move or label the v1 file as superseded.

finding: The 'base_rate_brier' column is an oracle: it uses the test season's own win rate, so it can't be known in advance. The statement 'little skill beyond the base rate' relies on it.
evidence: step1a_wp_eval.csv 2026 innings 1: LR 0.2404, oracle constant 0.2278, prior-seasons constant (batting-first win rate 0.505 in 2022-25) 0.2479. 2023 innings 1: LR 0.2476 vs prior constant 0.2500. 2026 batting-first win rate was 0.359 vs 0.49-0.55 in earlier seasons.
suggested_fix: Rename to 'oracle_season_rate_brier' and add a prior-seasons constant baseline. Say in the checkpoint that 2026 innings-1 skill is marginal and the base rate shifted.

finding: Brier and calibration intervals resample whole matches, which is correct, but hold the fitted model fixed. They ignore model-fit uncertainty, which is large for 2023 (67 training matches). Calibration uses 300 resamples against 1,000 for Brier.
evidence: step1a_winprob.py brier_ci (rng.integers over matches; 1000 draws) and calibration loop (rng.choice(mids), 300 draws).
suggested_fix: Add a note that the intervals cover test-match sampling only, or bootstrap the training matches as well for 2023-24.

finding: Step 1 asks for a calibration chart; only a table exists, and outputs/figures is empty.
evidence: outputs/figures is empty; step1a_calibration.csv only.
suggested_fix: Produce the chart (predicted vs observed with the 80% intervals, one panel per season).

finding: K_REF_BALLS = 240 in D27 was chosen after seeing the High shares in the scored seasons. The code comment says 2,400 left 2024 at 10.5%.
evidence: step1b_pressure.py comment above K_REF_BALLS. It does not leak future data (verified), but it is a tuning knob set on the outcome distribution. Strict D18 shares were 17.6 / 4.8 / 8.5 / 15.5%.
suggested_fix: State this tuning in D27 as a design choice made after seeing the shares. Show that the bucket composition by innings (see the finding above) is not hidden by it.

finding: The Step 2 opposition factor adds no accuracy out of sample and is only a team-level, venue-confounded proxy. The checkpoint still reports it as an adjustment, and its mean is 0.999 not 1.000 in 2023 and 2024.
evidence: MSE of bat runs per ball faced, 2023-26 (66,914 balls): cell only 3.25159; cell x opp 3.25333 (worse); cell x season 3.24580; full 3.24785 (worse than cell x season). Bowlers: cell x season 3.15063, full 3.15080. SD of opp factor 0.035 / 0.040. opp_bowl_f mean by season: 0.999 (2023), 0.999 (2024), 1.000, 1.000.
suggested_fix: Say the opposition factor has no measured predictive value; keep it for fairness only if the intervals in Step 4 show that it matters, or drop it. Use '~1.00' in the checkpoint.

finding: The Step 2 benchmark has a positive bias against batters every season, because the cells pool all earlier seasons with equal weight. It is disclosed (R14), but the size relative to expected player-level differences is not.
evidence: step2_season_offsets.csv: mean RAE 2023 +0.0186, 2024 +0.0398, 2025 +0.0044, 2026 +0.0165 per ball faced (1.9 to 4.0 runs per 100 balls). Phase x season: 2024 Death +0.057, 2025 Powerplay -0.011, 2026 Death +0.047. Per-match mean RAE SD 0.186/ball.
suggested_fix: Quote the offsets next to the typical size of High-pressure player RAE per 100 balls, so the reader can see what is noise.

finding: Leverage outcome classes are crude for no-balls, wides and wickets: the 'extra' class counts +1 run and no ball used, whatever the ball produced (no-ball + 6, wide + 4). A wicket always uses a ball and scores 0 (stumping off a wide is not a legal ball).
evidence: step1b_pressure.py outcome_class(): any wide/no-ball without a wicket is 'extra'; O_RUNS['extra'] = 1. Extras are about 4.5% of balls (3,552 wides + 380 no-ball types); 380 no-ball types carry 585 bat runs.
suggested_fix: Document it as an approximation, or split 'extra' into wide (+1) and no-ball (+1 + bat runs distribution).

finding: Checkpoint 1 describes the 2022 reference slightly wrongly, and it has no accuracy figure for the reference models.
evidence: step1a_ref2022_coverage.csv: 52 scored, 22 unscored. These are the first 20 matches (REF2022_MIN_PRIOR = 20) plus two ineligible matches (14130, 14164), not 'the first 22'. Reference Brier (my computation): innings 1 0.2083, innings 2 0.1363 (6,489 / 6,103 balls). These were trained with 20 to 68 earlier matches, and each match uses its own model.
suggested_fix: Fix the wording; add the reference Brier to step1a_wp_eval.

finding: pressure_ball.parquet keeps the hindsight columns next to the main index and the 2022 reference rows.
evidence: Columns: close_game_last5, pi_close, pi_close_bucket; 12,592 reference_only rows. step34_score.py uses pi_close only inside the with_close_game comparison and filters seasons 2023-26, so no leak today, but a single wrong column choice would break D8 and D18.
suggested_fix: Write the hindsight and reference columns to a separate comparison file, or prefix them (hindsight_...).

finding: Bucket thresholds (High >= 80, Medium 50-80, Low < 50) are not justified in one line each as the master prompt asks.
evidence: step1b_pressure.py docstring and PREREGISTRATION section 2 give the thresholds but not the reasons.
suggested_fix: Add one line for each threshold (for example High = top fifth of balls, in line with the master prompt's example).

finding: Bowler RSE and WAE are per delivery (wides and no-balls included), while Part 5 says that overs and economy use legal balls. 'Per 100 balls' in Steps 3-4 may therefore be ambiguous.
evidence: step2_expected.py: bowler rows are all deliveries (d = b.copy()); step2_season_offsets deliveries = 17,863 for 2023 vs legal balls less.
suggested_fix: State the unit in the glossary: 'per 100 deliveries' or convert to legal balls.
